q: The three elements of the fraud triangle described in SA 240 are:
o: Motive, means and materiality of the fraud committed
Collusion, concealment and override of the controls
Incentive or pressure, opportunity, rationalisation
Deficiency, deviation and resulting misstatement
why: SA 240 describes incentive or pressure, a perceived opportunity arising from weak controls or the ability to override them, and an attitude or rationalisation that lets the person justify the act.

q: Which statement about the presumption of fraud risk in revenue recognition under SA 240 is correct?
o: It is rebuttable and the reasons must be documented
It is irrebuttable and always a significant risk area
It applies only to listed entities and their subsidiaries
It applies only where revenue exceeds overall materiality
why: SA 240 requires the auditor to presume fraud risk in revenue recognition and evaluate which types of revenue give rise to it; the presumption may be rebutted only with documented reasons.

q: The primary distinction between fraudulent financial reporting and misappropriation of assets is that:
o: Fraudulent financial reporting is committed only by employees
Misappropriation always causes a material misstatement
Fraudulent reporting never involves concealment of any kind
Reporting fraud deceives users; misappropriation is theft
why: Fraudulent reporting is usually by management to deceive users about performance, whereas misappropriation is typically by employees and hidden by false records even where amounts are immaterial.

q: Which approach to selecting journal entries is most responsive to management override risk under SA 240?
o: Unusual accounts, period end postings and round sum entries
A random sample drawn from all entries posted in the year
Only entries with a value above the overall materiality level
Only entries reviewed and approved by the finance head
why: SA 240 directs selection on characteristics indicating inappropriate entries because override typically uses unusual, late, unsupported or round sum entries that random or value based selection would miss.

q: Which best describes the auditor responsibility for fraud under SA 240?
o: To detect every fraud in the entity regardless of amount
To certify that no fraud occurred during the financial year
To act as forensic investigator on any fraud risk factor
To obtain reasonable assurance about material misstatement
why: The auditor gives reasonable and not absolute assurance and the risk of not detecting fraud is higher than for error because of concealment and collusion; prevention and detection rest primarily with management and those charged with governance.

q: Under section 143 12 read with the rules, an auditor with reason to believe a fraud of one crore or above has been committed by officers or employees must:
o: Report direct to the Registrar of Companies within thirty days
Board or Audit Committee in two days, then Central Government
Deal with the matter only through CARO in the audit report
Report the matter to the Serious Fraud Office immediately
why: The prescribed route is a two day report to the Board or Audit Committee, a forty five day window for their reply, and onward reporting to the Central Government within fifteen days of receiving or not receiving that reply.

q: For a suspected fraud below the threshold specified under section 143 12, the auditor is required to:
o: No action is needed since the amount is below the legal limit
Report to the Central Government in the same way as larger frauds
Report to the Audit Committee or Board and in the Board report
Qualify the audit opinion in every such case of suspected fraud
why: Frauds below the specified threshold are reported to the Audit Committee or Board rather than to the Central Government, and the rules require prescribed particulars in the Board report.

q: The most important reason SA 240 mandates an engagement team discussion about fraud is to:
o: To allocate the audit work efficiently among team members
To document compliance with firm quality control policies
To agree materiality levels for fraud sensitive accounts
To exchange ideas on where the statements are vulnerable
why: The discussion is a brainstorming requirement centred on susceptibility to fraud and on how management might override controls, reinforcing scepticism; efficiency and materiality are separate planning matters.

q: A fraud risk factor was identified but the auditor concluded no material misstatement arose. SA 240 documentation then requires:
o: No documentation at all, as the conclusion reached was clean
Assessed fraud risks, responses and communications made
Only a brief note in the audit completion memorandum
Evidence only where the risk factor concerned revenue
why: SA 240 sets specific documentation requirements covering risks, responses, communications and rebuttal reasoning irrespective of the eventual conclusion reached.

q: Which circumstance most strongly indicates an incentive or pressure fraud risk factor for fraudulent financial reporting?
o: A high volume of manual journal entries in the ledger
Segregation of duties weaknesses in the stores department area
Pay tied to profit targets with a covenant breach looming
Absence of any internal audit function within the entity
why: Pay tied to aggressive targets combined with covenant pressure is a classic incentive factor; manual entries, weak segregation and no internal audit are opportunity factors instead.

q: If the auditor identifies a fraud involving senior management, SA 240 requires communication:
o: Timely to governance, with any regulatory duty considered
Only to the level of management immediately above those involved
Only through the written representation letter obtained
Only after the audit report has been signed and issued
why: Fraud involving management, employees with significant control roles, or fraud causing material misstatement must be reported to those charged with governance on a timely basis, and statutory duties under section 143 12 must also be weighed.

q: Management override of controls is treated as a risk present in every entity primarily because:
o: All managements are presumed to lack integrity until tested
Automated controls can never be overridden by any person
Segregation of duties is impossible in a smaller entity
Management can manipulate records and override controls
why: SA 240 treats override as an unpredictable risk in all entities because of the position management occupies, without presuming dishonesty, and requires specific procedures regardless of the view taken on integrity.

q: Which procedure specifically addresses the risk of management bias in accounting estimates as required by SA 240?
o: A retrospective review of prior period estimates for bias
Recalculating depreciation from the fixed asset register
Obtaining bank confirmations for all the operating accounts
Verifying the mathematical accuracy of the trial balance
why: SA 240 requires a retrospective review of the judgements and assumptions behind prior period estimates to detect a pattern of bias; the other procedures address quite different assertions.

q: Unusual or unexplained relationships noted while performing analytical procedures near the end of the audit should be:
o: Ignored where the accounts were already tested substantively
Reported directly to the Central Government without more work
Evaluated for whether they signal an unrecognised fraud risk
Resolved by obtaining a written representation from management
why: SA 240 requires evaluation of whether late stage analytical procedures reveal a previously unrecognised fraud risk; a representation is not sufficient evidence to resolve such an indicator.

q: The auditor concludes that a material misstatement from fraud makes continuing the engagement impossible. The most appropriate course under SA 240 is to:
o: Resign at once without any further communication to anyone
Issue an unmodified opinion with an emphasis of matter paragraph
Continue the audit while restricting the remaining scope
Weigh legal duties, inform governance and consider withdrawal
why: SA 240 requires determining professional and legal responsibilities, communicating with those charged with governance and any regulator, and where withdrawal is possible discussing and reporting the reasons; statutory duties survive resignation.

q: Which is the clearest example of an opportunity fraud risk factor rather than an attitude or rationalisation?
o: Management justifying aggressive accounting as immaterial
Domination by one individual without effective oversight
A known history of securities law violations by management
Management showing excessive interest in the share price
why: Domination by one person without effective oversight combined with unusual related party transactions creates the opportunity to commit and conceal fraud; the others describe attitudes, rationalisations or incentives.

q: The auditor identifies a misstatement that may indicate fraud although the amount is immaterial. SA 240 requires the auditor to:
o: Disregard it because it falls below the materiality level
Deal with it through CARO reporting in the audit report
Adjust the statements without any further procedures
Evaluate its implications, as fraud is rarely isolated
why: SA 240 states fraud is seldom an isolated occurrence, so even an immaterial indicator requires reassessment of risks, the reliability of evidence and representations, and possibly the whole approach.

q: Written representations obtained under SA 240 include management acknowledgement that:
o: The statements contain no fraud of any amount whatsoever
Responsibility for controls and disclosure of known fraud
The auditor bears responsibility for detecting entity fraud
The entity has never faced any regulatory inquiry at all
why: SA 240 requires representations covering responsibility for controls, the results of the management fraud risk assessment and disclosure of known, suspected or alleged fraud; absolute assurance that no fraud exists cannot be given.
